SSME blades are subject to severe thermal, pressure, and forced vibration environments.
SSME/STAEBL is a stand-alone code for the automated design of SSME turbopump blades.
The SSME/STAEBL code was developed by systematically modifying and enhancing the STAEBL (Structural Tailoring of Engine Blades) code.

Additions and modifications to the STAEBL code include thermal stress analysis, gas dynamic (pressure) loads, temperature-dependent material and thermal properties, forced vibrations, and blade cross-section stacking offsets.
Optimization studies showed that the additional thermal and pressure loads, as well as temperature-dependent properties, require additional weight in the optimized SSME blade design.
For the blade designs dominated by root stress constraints, the crystal axis orientation was found to have a relatively insignificant effect on the optimal design.
Blade cross-section stacking offsets were shown to have a very significant effect on root stress-dominated SSME blade designs.
The initial SSME blade design violated the root stress constraint, which is extremely sensitive to the offset variables.
The optimized SSME blade design recommended a significant change in blade stacking to meet the root stress constraint.
Structural optimization provides a practical and flexible approach to SSME blade design, allowing the incorporation of many design variables, constraints, loads, and analysis options.
Typical design variables for SSME blade optimization include blade thickness distribution and root chord.
Typical constraints for SSME blade optimization include resonance margins, root stress, root-to-chord ratios, and tip displacement.
The SSME/STAEBL code includes capabilities for data transfer from finite element models and stand-alone analysis.
Optimization studies were undertaken to assess the influence of blade cross-section offsets on the optimal SSME blade design.

The difference between the designs optimized under centrifugal loads only and under centrifugal, thermal, and pressure loads with temperature-dependent blade properties can be attributed to material property temperature dependence.
